tasks.answer: Top hit and exact match. Export FlightDelayCompensationBatchScreen; summary: "Batch compensation workspace for standard, special and review steps." Constraint: batchId is required and the screen needs query/auth/router providers and handles offline/conflict states.

Only one catalog entry matched: the generic traveler booking list (paginated, with search and filters). No dedicated "special traveler" (特殊旅客) booking-list variant was returned; get confirmed the entry has no variants and props are initialStatus (optional) and navigate (required). If a special-traveler-specific screen exists, it is not exposed under this ID in the catalog.

Password field with show/hide labels and a form-field error. It has no required props. Error display: the component must be used inside UiFormField, and error is a string prop that the field wrapper (UiFormField) renders below the input; PasswordInput itself does not render the error message.

The single --layer auto search surfaced only the composite travelers booking list screen (summary: "Paginated traveler booking list with search and filters", required prop navigate). It did not return standalone search-bar or filter-panel entries, so two component IDs could not be produced within the one-search budget. The search/filter UI appears to be internal to that screen, or its standalone components live in another layer that layer auto (inferred feature) excluded.

Global dialog that subscribes to the auth recovery store and lazily renders its view. Mount it once near the app root; it renders null while no recovery event is pending. No required props. (Its view component is common.AuthRecoveryDialogView, which requires detail.)

notes: All 5 searches ran from /tmp/oss-trial/airport-mobile with --layer auto and --limit 5 --details (no manual --layer), logging to /tmp/audit-airport-layer-auto/usage/catalog-2.jsonl. Layer inference per search: task1 feature/layerSource=auto; task2 feature/auto; task3 feature/auto; task4 feature/auto; task5 shared-ui/auto. In every case the returned layer equaled the top-ranked hit layer, and the result set contained only that layer, so auto behaves as a layer filter keyed off the first hit. Task 5 flipped to shared-ui cleanly. Task 4 was the only miss: with the layer pinned to feature it returned just the composite TravelerBookingListScreen (1 item, 0 omitted), so the standalone search-bar and filter-panel components were not observable; a manual/shared-ui layer pass would likely be needed to identify them. One get was used on bookings.TravelerBookingListScreen (task 2) to confirm required props and the absence of a special-traveler variant. No project files were read or modified; nothing under /tmp/oss-trial/airport-mobile changed.
